Expectation1: Look out for each other's safety and well-being
Situation1: One sibling is preparing to try a new skateboard trick on a steep, uneven ramp.
Situation2: Your friend has misunderstood the tone of your text message and replied sounding hurt. You need to call them right now to explain.
Story: I stood at the edge of the skate park, my phone buzzing insistently in my pocket. My stepbrother, Jamie, was tightening his helmet, eyes fixed on the steep, cracked ramp. He grinned at me, excitement and nerves mixing in his expression. I knew he’d been practicing this trick for weeks, but the ramp looked even rougher today, and I remembered Mom’s words: “Look out for each other.” I wanted to tell him to wait, to check the ramp again, to be careful. But my phone vibrated again—my best friend, Sam. I’d sent a rushed text earlier, and now Sam’s reply was sharp, hurt. I could hear the disappointment in their words, and I knew I needed to call, to explain, to fix things before the misunderstanding grew. Jamie was already rolling toward the ramp, and I felt torn in two—my responsibility to keep him safe pulling me one way, my loyalty to Sam tugging the other. My heart pounded as I tried to decide which role I couldn’t let down.
